items.actClause:
AN ACT creating a temporary state commission relating to local correctional
facilities in upstate New York; and providing for the repeal of such
provisions upon expiration thereof
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S2169

SPONSOR: BAILEY
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act creating a temporary state commission relating to local correc-
tional facilities in upstate New York; and providing for the repeal of
such provisions upon expiration thereof

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA:

This bill creates a three-year commission to study local jails outside
of New York City, with particular emphasis on conditions of confinement
including, but not limited to, medical and mental health care, over-
crowding, inmate inmate deaths, use of restraints, use of force and
segregated confinement.

 
SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:

Section 1. establishes a temporary state commission on local jails to
study and make recommendations for statewide policy or reforms, specif-
ically focusing on mental health care, medical treatment, overcrowding,
restraints, inmate deaths, the use of force and segregated confinement.

Section 2. prescribes the manner in which eleven commission members will
be appointed.

Section 3. provides that commission members will receive no compen-
sation, but will be reimbursed for their expenses pertaining to the
performance of their duties.

Section 4. grants commission members unrestricted access to all local
correctional facilities across the state. Access includes the ability to
conduct confidential interviews of inmates and employee and unredacted
copies of dccuments. The commission is instructed to hold public hear-
ings with all the powers of a legislative committee.

Section 5. provides for reports by the commission to the governor and
legislature.

Section 6. establishes an effective date and repeal date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

While the crime rate has fallen across the state in the last several
years, overcrowding in some county jails remains a problem.  Addi-
tionally, county jails often have trouble finding and retaining medical
and mental health staff or contractors and may lack the resources to
provide mentally ill or drug addicted inmates with effective treatment
or programming. Each county jail has different problems and policies and
must remain responsive to unique local concerns.

Even though the State Commission of Correction, itselfunddrfunded and
understaffed, has oversight authority of the county jails, it only
establishes minimum standards for jails and does not otherwise develop
coordinated policy on conditions of confinement, programming, use of
force and medical and mental health care.


This bill would provide for a temporary commission appointed. by the
governor and legislature to review the conditions in local jails outside
of New York City, report on their findings, make recommendations for
statewide policy or reforms that might be needed to provide for humane
and uniform treatment of jail inmates across the various counties, and
identify problems that may require state funding, legislation or other
state action to help sheriffs improve jail conditions. The commission
would have unfettered access to jails across the state and would hold
public hearingS in a number of regional centers in order to receive
input from all stakeholders in the local county jails prior to issuing
its final report.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2017-18: A.7959 (Weprin) - Referred to Correction

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

To be determined.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately and shall expire and be deemed
repealed three years after such date.

summary: Creates a temporary state commission relating to local correctional facilities in upstate New York; emphasis shall be placed on medical and mental health care, overcrowding, inmate deaths, use of force, restraints, and all segregation and confinement practices and solitary confinement.
